where: crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/unit/compile.rs pin_kept and sealed, serve/unit/deps.rs store, crates/hir-def/src/deps/key.rs sealed_in
what: Whether a crate is built once a machine was decided in four places by four rules: the package name "bstd" (pin_kept, deps::store), a crate origin that is not local (hir_def::deps::sealed), and a shipped tree under the manifest dir (compile::sealed). A registry crate and a git dependency at a locked commit were sealed in one place and not another, so their front-end records went to the home while their units' records went to the layer.
cost: every home rebuilt the front end of every registry crate; no daemon of a second home could reuse a sealed crate whole
cause: sealing was inferred where it was needed from whatever that code had at hand (a name, an origin) instead of being a fact the planner records once
class: a property recomputed at each use site from proxies instead of stated once at its source
prevention: one rule in serve::sealed::pin (a digest that pins the tree: shipped, registry checksum, git locked commit), recorded by the planner as CrateData::sealed and read by everyone else; the name checks are deleted
fix: serve::sealed::pin; Lower::sealed and CrateData::sealed; hir_def::deps::sealed_in reads the pin only; KeptPut::into routes a sealed crate's records to the layer, waited on with the layer's own durable. Tests: a_package_is_sealed_exactly_when_a_digest_pins_its_tree, a_crate_is_sealed_by_its_pin_and_nothing_else, a_sealed_crate_one_home_built_on_the_machine_layer_another_home_builds_none_of (controls: the origin rule; records routed to the home).
